new.title: Feed the sacred carp at Balıklıgöl
new.desc: Balıklıgöl is the pool at the heart of old Urfa, tied to the legend of Abraham being cast from the citadel into a fire that turned to water. Its carp are considered sacred and are not eaten. Colonnades and mosques frame the water, with the Rızvaniye reflected on its north side.
new.tip: Come at dusk, when the pool is lit and locals gather; fish food is sold at stalls. Modest dress is expected near the shrines.
new.q: Balıklıgöl, Halil-ür Rahman Gölü, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Visit the Halil-ür Rahman Mosque and Dergah
new.desc: The Halil-ür Rahman Mosque stands at the west end of the Balıklıgöl pool, in a complex of courtyards and arcades known as the Dergah. Sources date the mosque to 1211, when the Ayyubids converted an earlier church. It is the most visited place in the city.
new.tip: Remove shoes and dress modestly; avoid prayer times. The courtyard has a stall selling prayer beads and scents.
new.q: Halil-ür Rahman Camii, Dergah, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: See the Mevlid-i Halil cave where Abraham is said to be born
new.desc: Believers hold that Abraham was born in this cave on the slope below the castle, in the north-west of the Dergah complex. The adjoining Mevlid-i Halil Mosque has a courtyard and gate built in 1947, and the cave is entered through a separate prayer hall.
new.tip: Visit in the morning to avoid queues; men and women use separate entrances to the cave.
new.q: Mevlid-i Halil Camii, Dergah, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Admire the Rızvaniye Mosque and Medrese above the pool
new.desc: The Rızvaniye Mosque and its medrese were built on the north side of Halil-ür Rahman Lake in the 18th century, reportedly on the site of an earlier church. Its cloisters and the mosque's reflection in the water are among the best-known views of Balıklıgöl.
new.tip: Walk the northern promenade for the reflection photograph; best in morning or evening light.
new.q: Rızvaniye Camii, Halil-ür Rahman Gölü, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Meet the Balıklıgöl Man at the Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum
new.desc: One of Türkiye's largest museums, it opened in 2015 on Haleplibahçe street. Its star is the Balıklıgöl Man, described as one of the oldest known life-size human statues, alongside finds from Göbeklitepe and Karahantepe and Assyrian, Hittite and Roman pieces.
new.tip: Allow two or three hours; the Neolithic galleries are the highlight. Check opening days locally.
new.q: Şanlıurfa Arkeoloji Müzesi, Haleplibahçe Caddesi, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Walk over Roman floors at the Haleplibahçe Mosaic Museum
new.desc: The mosaic museum protects Roman villa floors left where they were found, under a large roof at Haleplibahçe. Highlights include the Orpheus mosaic dated AD 194 and the Hunting Amazons panel, thought to be 5th or 6th century.
new.tip: A short walk from Balıklıgöl. Flooding once hit the site, so check it is open before going.
new.q: Haleplibahçe Mozaik Müzesi, Haleplibahçe Caddesi, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Find the clock-tower minaret of the Urfa Ulu Cami
new.desc: The Ulu Cami in Camikebir quarter dates to the 12th century (Lonely Planet gives 1170-75) and is built in the Syrian tradition on the site of an earlier church. A clock was added to its minaret in the Republican period, making it the city's only clock tower.
new.tip: Enter the courtyard modestly dressed outside prayer times; it lies next to the covered bazaars.

new.title: See the Selahaddin Eyyubi Mosque, once a church
new.desc: Planetware calls it the city's most beautiful mosque. It was built over the Church of St John the Baptist and has since been restored. Its stonework and courtyard show the layered Christian and Islamic history of Urfa.
new.tip: Dress modestly; combine with a walk through the old streets around Balıklıgöl.

new.title: Study the stonework of the Hasan Padişah Mosque
new.desc: Built in two phases, the front single-domed part by a Turkish bey and the main building in 1499 by Şeyh Yakup, known as Uzun Hasan of the Akkoyunlu. The cut-stone mosque stands near Balıklıgöl in the Akarbaşı area.
new.tip: Quiet and rarely crowded; combine with a visit to the lake area.
new.q: Hasan Padişah Camii, Akarbaşı, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Spot the church-turned-mosque Fırfırlı Camii
new.desc: Fırfırlı Camii began as the First Armenian Evangelical Church of Urfa in the 19th century and was converted to a mosque in 1956. Tradition says the Varak cross, brought to Urfa in 1092, was found here.
new.tip: Best seen from outside; a quick stop on a walk through the old town.

new.title: Step into the Reji Church of St Peter and St Paul
new.desc: The Reji Church was built in 1861 on the remains of a 6th-century church and has since been revived as a cultural venue. It stands north-east of Ellisekiz Meydanı in Kurtuluş quarter.
new.tip: Opening is irregular as a cultural venue; ask at the adjoining Reji boutique hotel.

new.title: Learn Urfa cooking at the Kitchen Museum in Hacıbanlar House
new.desc: The municipality bought the historic Hacıbanlar House in 2011 and restored it as a museum of Urfa's culinary heritage. Rooms show old kitchen equipment and traditional cooking tools in a restored early-20th-century stone konak.
new.tip: Shows how the city's dishes were made at home; pair it with a lunch stop nearby.
new.q: Şanlıurfa Mutfak Müzesi, Hacıbanlar Konağı, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: See Urfa Castle and its columns above the old town
new.desc: Urfa Castle stands on Dambak Tepesi south of Balıklıgöl, with Corinthian columns tied to the legend of Abraham's trial. Excavations by Prof. Gülriz Kozbe's team have run for six years, with the governor aiming to reopen it to visitors by the end of 2026.
new.tip: Interior access is currently limited; check the latest status and view it from the Gölbaşı side.
new.q: Urfa Kalesi, Dambak Tepesi, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Explore the Roman rock tombs of Kızılkoyun Necropolis
new.desc: The Kızılkoyun Necropolis is a 5-hectare site on Tılfındır Hill north of the city centre. It has more than 50 Roman-period rock-cut tombs with inscriptions, reliefs and mosaics, opened to visitors as an open-air museum.
new.tip: Wear sturdy shoes; check opening hours as access has changed with restoration.

new.title: Visit the Eyyüb Peygamber Sabır Makamı and its healing well
new.desc: South of the centre, the complex of the Prophet Job (Eyyüb) includes the Çile Mağarası and a spring believed to have sprung when he struck the ground. It is a pilgrimage site in the Eyyüb Peygamber neighbourhood.
new.tip: Dress modestly; it is a quiet, local-feeling stop away from the Balıklıgöl crowds.
new.q: Hz. Eyyüb Sabır Makamı, Eyyüb Peygamber Mahallesi, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: See the 1903 Hacı Kamil Konağı
new.desc: This stone mansion was built in 1903 by Hacı Yusuf Kâmil at a reported cost of 12,000 gold coins. The municipality bought and restored it with local stone, and it is lit at night as a heritage landmark.
new.tip: Photograph it in the evening light; check whether it is open to enter.

new.title: Watch the reflections on Ayn-ı Zeliha Lake
new.desc: Ayn-ı Zeliha is the lake south of Halil-ür Rahman, in front of the castle. Legend says it formed where Nimrod's daughter Zeliha fell after being thrown into the fire.
new.tip: Quieter than the main pool; stroll the edge at sunset.

new.title: Eat ciğer kebab at Meşhur Ciğerci Aziz Usta
new.desc: A busy ciğer grill in the Pınarbaşı area of Eyyübiye, serving skewered lamb liver with onions, tomatoes and pide from a charcoal fire. The menu also includes lahmacun, and it opens from 5 am to 2 am.
new.tip: Order a ciğer dürüm or plate; liver is traditionally eaten for breakfast in Urfa.
new.q: Meşhur Ciğerci Aziz Usta, Pınarbaşı Mahallesi, 1211. Sokak, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Try fındık lahmacun at Sultanoğlu Kebap Pide Lahmacun
new.desc: Sultanoğlu in Haliliye bakes lahmacun in hot, mild and the thicker local fındık style alongside pide, kebab and ocakbaşı dishes. Reviewers praise how evenly the meat and onion are spread.
new.tip: Try the fındık lahmacun with a side of ayran.
new.q: Sultanoğlu Kebap Pide Lahmacun, Karşıyaka Mahallesi, Haliliye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Dine in the courtyard of Cevahir Han
new.desc: Cevahir Han is a historic caravanserai turned restaurant in the north of the old walled city, near the former Samsat gate. It serves Urfa dishes such as borani and çiğ köfte (ordered for groups) and hosts evening sıra nights.
new.tip: Book ahead for çiğ köfte, which needs five or more people.
new.q: Cevahir Han, Samsat Kapı, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Eat Urfa-style çiğ köfte at Battalbey
new.desc: Battalbey is described as one of the city's oldest çiğ köfte shops, preparing the traditional Urfa version in meat and meat-free forms.
new.tip: Eat it wrapped in lettuce with pomegranate molasses.

new.title: Order Urfa kebab at the Altın Lokantası
new.desc: Altın Lokantası is cited in several local guides for traditional Urfa food, including kebab with special spices and breakfast.
new.tip: Go for the Urfa kebab and local appetisers.

new.title: Sip tea or menengiç coffee at Gümrük Hanı
new.desc: Gümrük Hanı, built in 1563 by Halhallı Behram Paşa, is a caravanserai with a courtyard under old plane trees where locals play dominoes and okey. Water from Halil-ür Rahman passes through the court, and menengiç coffee topped with pistachios is served.
new.tip: Order tea, menengiç or the bitter mırra coffee in the courtyard.
new.q: Gümrük Hanı, Pınarbaşı Mahallesi, Eyyübiye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Eat patlıcan kebabı and şıllık at Şehr-i Urfa
new.desc: Şehr-i Urfa on Haleplibahçe Caddesi serves lahmacun, Urfa kebab and eggplant kebab and is known for meal-and-music sıra nights.
new.tip: Finish with the warm walnut şıllık dessert.

new.title: Have breakfast with fried isot at Şehrazat Konağı
new.desc: Şehrazat Konağı is a historic stone mansion serving classic breakfast alongside local dishes such as paçanga böreği and fried isot.
new.tip: Ask for the fried isot with eggs.

new.title: Taste Urfa pistachio ice cream at Miroğlu
new.desc: Miroğlu is known for ice cream made with local Urfa pistachios.
new.tip: Order pistachio after a bazaar walk.
new.q: Miroğlu Kadayıf & Dondurma, Emniyet Caddesi, Haliliye, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Browse shawls and kilims in the Kazzaz Bedesten
new.desc: The Kazzaz Bedesten, a covered market dated to 1562, stands beside Gümrük Hanı and sells shawls, traditional clothing, carpets, copperware and local goods such as isot and pomegranate molasses.
new.tip: Haggle politely and drink tea nearby.

new.title: Watch coppersmiths in the Bakırcılar Çarşısı
new.desc: The Hüseyniye or Bakırcılar Çarşısı, built in 1887, was once a carpet market and now houses coppersmiths who make kettles, trays, ibriks and samovars.
new.tip: Ask the makers about the craft.

new.title: Buy isot at the Hamarat Eller Çarşısı
new.desc: The Hamarat Eller market is where local women sell isot, tomato paste and dried goods.
new.tip: Taste before buying isot.
new.q: Hamarat Eller Çarşısı, Şanlıurfa Merkez, Şanlıurfa

new.title: Join a sıra gecesi at Hayatlı Konak
new.desc: Hayatlı Konak is a restored stone mansion that offers sıra gecesi programmes nightly: music, folk songs and local food in a historic setting.
new.tip: Reserve ahead.

new.title: Bathe in the restored Vezir Hamamı
new.desc: The Vezir Hamamı is a historic Ottoman bath that operated as a public bath for centuries and reopened after restoration in 2015.
new.tip: Check opening and gender hours.

new.title: Watch the lights from Maşuk Seyir Tepesi
new.desc: Maşuk Seyir Tepesi is a viewpoint with different views by day and night, called one of the city's most romantic spots.
new.tip: Go at sunset.

new.title: Visit the Kuşçu Pazarı bird market
new.desc: Kuşçu Pazarı is a bird market where birds are sold at night auctions with heated bargaining.
new.tip: Visit in the evening.
